definitions.explanation: Items that are no longer useful in their current form and have been discarded or set aside for disposal, recycling, or repurposing.

examples.japanese: {廃品|はいひん}{回収|かいしゅう}は{毎月|まいつき}{第|だい}{一|いち}{土曜日|どようび}です。
examples.english: Scrap collection is on the first Saturday of every month.

examples.japanese: {廃品|はいひん}を{利用|りよう}してアートを{作|つく}る。
examples.english: To make art using discarded materials.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}の{廃品|はいひん}{回収|かいしゅう}で{古新聞|ふるしんぶん}や{段|だん}ボールを{集|あつ}めた。
examples.english: We collected old newspapers and cardboard in the school's scrap drive.

notes:
A compound of {廃|はい} (waste, discard) + {品|ひん} (goods, items). Most commonly appears in the phrase {廃品回収|はいひんかいしゅう} (scrap/waste collection).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {廃品|はいひん}{回収|かいしゅう}: scrap collection, waste collection drive
- {廃品|はいひん}{回収|かいしゅう}{業者|ぎょうしゃ}: scrap collector, junk dealer
- {廃品|はいひん}を{集|あつ}める: to collect scrap/waste
- {廃品|はいひん}{利用|りよう}: reuse of waste materials

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, {廃品回収|はいひんかいしゅう} (scrap collection drives) are commonly organized by neighborhood associations, schools, or community groups as fundraising activities. Old newspapers, magazines, cardboard, and aluminum cans are typical items collected.

RELATED WORDS:
- {廃棄物|はいきぶつ}: waste, refuse — more formal/technical term for waste in general
- {粗大|そだい}ゴミ: oversized garbage — large items like furniture that require special disposal
- {不用品|ふようひん}: unwanted items — things no longer needed but not necessarily waste
